country.name: Sweden
country.tagline: Skåne's southern hills and Baltic islands are making a new wine story at 56 degrees north.
country.overview: Sweden's wine-growing is a twenty-first-century story, made possible by warmer summers and fungus-resistant grapes. The main area is Skåne, the southernmost province, where vineyards grow on the Kullaberg peninsula near Arild, around Österlen and near Malmö and Lund; there are also vineyards on Gotland and Öland in the Baltic and along the west coast. Solaris dominates, with Rondo, Regent and some Pinot Noir and Chardonnay for sparkling. Kullabergs Vingård and Arilds Vingård on the Kullaberg peninsula, with sea-warmed slopes, are among the best known. Sweden has no EU-registered wine PDO in the dataset used here; any newly registered names should be checked in eAmbrosia.

history.title: Monastic vines
history.text: Monasteries in Skåne grew some vines in the Middle Ages, though wine-growing never became significant.

history.title: Modern start
history.text: Commercial vineyards appeared in Skåne in the early 2000s, helped by warmer summers and fungus-resistant varieties.

country.classification: No wine PDO is listed for Sweden in the EU geospatial dataset used for this atlas (Candiago et al. 2022). Wines are sold as Swedish wine without a protected origin unless a newer registration exists.
country.climate_soils: Cool maritime to continental with very long summer days. Skåne has fertile moraine and limestone; the Kullaberg is a granite and gneiss ridge warmed by the sea.

sources.title: Candiago et al. (2022), geospatial inventory of EU wine PDOs (registration dates, varieties, communes)

regions.name: Skåne
regions.tagline: Sweden's southern tip, where most of its vines grow.
regions.summary: Skåne, the southernmost Swedish province, has most of Sweden's vineyards, from the Kullaberg peninsula in the north-west to Österlen in the south-east.
regions.history: A modern development since the early 2000s.
regions.terroir: Moraine, limestone and granite; maritime influence.
regions.grapes: Solaris, Rondo, Regent, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay.

sources.title: Candiago et al. (2022), geospatial inventory of EU wine PDOs (registration dates, varieties, communes)

sites.name: Kullabergs Vingård
sites.text: A vineyard near Arild on the Kullaberg peninsula, on sea-warmed slopes facing the Kattegat.

sites.name: Arilds Vingård
sites.text: One of Sweden's best-known estates, at Brunnby near Arild on the Kullaberg, with sparkling and still wines.
